previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis and chronic abdominal pain was admitted with acute epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had a gastroparesis flare, with labs showing only mild lipase elevation, ruling out acute pancreatitis. Metoclopramide was avoided due to interaction risks with her venlafaxine. She was started on IV erythromycin, which improved her symptoms, allowing advancement to a regular diet. She was transitioned to oral erythromycin and discharged home in stable condition after six days. Follow-up was arranged with her primary care physician and gastroenterologist. Her anxiety, depression, and hearing impairment were acknowledged and accommodated throughout the stay.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with recurrent abdominal 
pain thought secondary to gastroparesis vs. sphincter of oddi

admissions, presenting with nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain 
and loose stool  

#  Abdominal pain/nausea vomiting/gastroparesis flare
The patient presented with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and 
loose stools, similar symptoms to her previous admissions for 
flares of gastroparesis. Her presentation as in the setting of 
recently restarting PO erythromycin after taking reglan during a 
1 week holiday off of erythromycin. There was no evidence of 
infection as the patient remained afebrile without leukocytosis 
throughout. Her abdominal exam remained benign throughout the 
admission as well. Her lipase was only mildly elevated to 73 on 
admission, and stable to 82 on recheck,  < 2x the upper limit of 
normal, suggesting against pancreatitis as the etiology. As 
gastroparesis was thought to be the underlying etiology the 
patient was started on IV erythromycin with meals, as well as IV 
dilaudid and IV phenergan. She slowly improved throughout the 
admission. The primary team contacted both Dr. ___, her 
gastroenterologist her primarily manages her gastroparesis, as 
well as her outside gastroenterologist Dr. ___. who 
primarily manages her pancreatitis. She was ultimately 
transitioned from IV medications back to PO erythromycin and 
anti nausea medications. Her abdominal pain was much improved on 
disccharge, and she was tolerating a liquid diet. She required 
no additional oral pain medications. Her home medications were 
otherwise continued as they were previous to the admission. 

# Hypotension
During the admission the patient had overnight and early morning 
low blood pressures with systolics running in the ___. The 
patient remained asymptomatic throughout, her pressures would 
improve with gentle 500 cc boluses of normal saline. This was 
thought multifactorial, with a contribution from her medications 
notably prazosin and dilaudid (which she would take at night) as 
well as due to decreased PO intake in the setting of her likely 
gastroparesis flare.

# Anxiety/Depression
The patient continued her home regimen of:
- Clonazepam 2 mg PO QHS
- Venlafazine XR 225 mg PO QAM
- Imipramine 20 mg PO QPM
- Prazosin 1 mg PO QPM 
- Gabapentin 200 gm QHS

# Allergies
